script.spoken: Water doesn't always freeze at 0 °C. Freezing needs a speck or surface to start on. Without one, water stays liquid below 0 °C. That's called supercooling. Tap a supercooled bottle, and it can freeze in seconds. Cooled fast enough, water becomes a glass near −137 °C. So 0 °C is when water can freeze, not when it must.
